findings.title: C16 groups records by source.sha256, so a quarterly file whose bytes did not change between quarters cannot be loaded for both quarters; following the README (GPCI2026.csv, no renaming) also silently overwrites the earlier quarter's draft
findings.problem: fileWindowProblems keys 'one file' on `${content} ${record.source.sha256}`. CMS ships the same GPCI file (and can ship an unchanged MUE table) in each quarterly zip. If the operator renames it so both quarters are kept (GPCI2026_Q1.csv, GPCI2026_Q2.csv), the bytes are the same and C16 refuses the drafts as 'records from one file carry different windows'. If the operator follows README row 2 and does not rename (GPCI2026.csv each quarter), storeSource accepts the identical bytes, and import.ts:365-368 writes content/drafts/pfs_gpci/2026/GPCI2026.json again, replacing the Q1 records with Q2's with no warning. That breaks the README's own 'Keep every quarter'. The only remaining workaround is to change the source bytes, which damages provenance. Nothing is priced wrong, because the coverage check and #7 catch the hole later, but the quarterly procedure #30 builds cannot be carried out for an unchanged GPCI.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds, and major is the right severity. I re-ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6dcacc47-f55b-5ed0-ab9e-d8b495c8bdd9/scratchpad/review-probes/probe1.mts against 45fe117f under the lock.

(1) Following the README exactly overwrites the earlier quarter. `fileWindowProblems` (tools/verify-content/check.ts:340-358) groups records by `${content} ${record.source.sha256}`. README row 2 (content/sources/README.md, table row 2) gives `--file GPCI2026.csv`, with no quarter token in the name. The quarter is taken from `--url` (rvu26a.zip, then rvu26b.zip), so both imports are accepted. `storeSource` (packages/rules/src/import.ts, about lines 287-303) lets the identical bytes through. `importRuleFile` then writes content/drafts/pfs_gpci/2026/GPCI2026.json with no check, both times. Probe case F shows both imports returning that same draft path, and afterwards the draft holds only 2026-04-01..2026-06-30. The Q1 records are gone with no warning, which breaks the README's own "Keep every quarter".

(2) Renaming each quarter's copy is refused instead. GPCI2026_Q1.csv and GPCI2026_Q2.csv have the same bytes. The name and the URL agree on the quarter, so both imports are accepted, but checkContentSet on content/drafts then returns "pfs_gpci records from one file (content/sources/pfs_gpci/GPCI2026_Q2.csv) carry different windows (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31 and 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30)...". That message tells the operator to "import it again", which is exactly what they just did.

So for any quarterly file CMS republishes unchanged, the procedure #30 builds cannot be carried out at all. GPCI is the realistic case: the same GPCI{year}.csv ships in every RVU zip of the year. The only workaround is to change the source bytes, which damages provenance.

The code follows the design's C16 row (design line 753 says "the same `source.sha256`"), so the defect is in the design as well as the implementation. It is not a blocker: nothing loads or prices unchecked. The coverage checks and #7 refuse the resulting gap, and C16 itself fails closed. It is a design requirement that cannot be met, plus silent data loss in drafts, which is what major means here.

2. In importRuleFile, add a refusal (inside #30's exception): before the writeFileSync of the draft, read any existing draft at that path. If it holds a different window, refuse with "<draft> already holds <window>; give this quarter's file its own name (e.g. GPCI2026_Q2.csv) so every quarter is kept". Overwriting the same window stays allowed, so a correction can still be re-imported.

findings.title: Nothing refuses a release number below the newest: it is compared against an older release, and the later published release then fails C8 permanently
findings.problem: assembleRelease refuses only a number already in use. If releases 1 and 3 exist, release 2 can be assembled. previousReleaseNumber(root, 2) is 1, so release 2 is compared against 1 and may drop anything release 3 covers. After that, the checker on content/outgoing/3, or on an immutable content/releases/3, reports C8 for good ('names previous release 1, but the release before 3 is 2'), and every PR's verify-content goes red with no way to fix a published release. D2 and A5 also disagree in this state: the note must name 1 for A5 but 3 for D2.
findings.evidence: probe1.mts case B: assemble 1 gives 'assembled content/outgoing/1'. Add the Q4 MUE and assemble 3: 'assembled content/outgoing/3'. Delete the Q4 draft and assemble 2: 'assembled content/outgoing/2' (no coverage refusal, although 3 covers Q4). checkContent(root, [], {today:'2026-10-26'}) then returns ["content/outgoing/3: COVERAGE.md names previous release 1, but the release before 3 is 2"].
findings.fix: In assembleRelease, before reading drafts, add a refusal when `previousReleaseNumber(root, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)` is >= release: 'release n not assembled: release m exists; a new release takes a number above the newest'. Give the checker the same rule: a numbered set below the highest number that has no COVERAGE.md predecessor chain is refused. Add a test.

verdict.reason: The mechanism holds at 45fe117f, but the consequence is overstated. The guard at tools/release/assemble.ts:411-416 only refuses a number already used in content/outgoing or content/releases. previousReleaseNumber (packages/rules/src/content.ts:178-194) returns the highest number below n. So with 1 and 3 present, `pnpm release:assemble 2` succeeds and release 2 is compared against 1. Then C8 in tools/verify-content/check.ts:552-553 flags release 3, because its COVERAGE.md names 1 while the release before 3 is now 2. The design (section 786) defines previous as 'highest number below n' and never requires numbers to go up, so this is a missing guard, not a broken design requirement. The 'permanently red on every PR' claim does not hold up. The bad state starts in the PR that adds content/outgoing/2. pnpm verify-content runs in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:92) and reports the C8 problem on 3 in that same PR, so the check fails closed before anything merges. Nothing loads or prices unchecked, and no published release has to change. The fix is to delete outgoing/2 and reassemble under 4. The permanent state needs someone to merge past a red required check, and the D2/A5 mismatch exists only in that same never-merged state. Reaching it at all also needs an operator to type a number below the newest, against the runbook's 'pnpm release:assemble <the next release number>' (docs/runbooks/content-updates.md:89). What is real: the tool accepts an out-of-order number without complaint, and CI then blames release 3 instead of the new release 2, which misleads. Rank it minor, a usability and guard defect, not major.
verdict.betterFix: In assembleRelease, after the 'already exists' loop, compute newest = previousReleaseNumber(root, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). If newest !== null && release <= newest, throw ReleaseToolError(`release ${release} not assembled: release ${newest} exists; a new release takes a number above the newest (${newest + 1})`). In the checker, so the error names the right directory: for each numbered set n in content/outgoing, if a set numbered m > n exists in content/releases or content/outgoing and m's COVERAGE.md names a previous release below n, report it on n, e.g. 'content/outgoing/2: release 3 already exists; a release number must be above the newest'. Add a release.test.ts case (assemble 1, assemble 3, assemble 2 throws) and a check.test.ts case for the out-of-order set.

findings.title: The checker never checks an RVU, GPCI or MUE record's window against the quarter its stored source states (only ZIP quotes are checked), so a whole file re-dated by hand to another quarter passes and assembles
findings.problem: statedWindowProblems checks only that the window lies inside some quarter (C1), plus the ZIP quote YYYYQ (C3). #30 R2 says the window is 'cross-checked against the quarter the file states'. For pfs_gpci and ncci_mue only the importer does that. A draft edit that moves every record of MUE_2026Q3.csv to 2026-10-01..2026-12-31 keeps C1, C15 and C16 happy, because all of them share one window. Q3's values then price Q4 lines. pfs_rvu is no better protected: its value.quarter is taken from the window start, so editing it alongside the dates passes the schema refinement. The edited records still need an L2 person, but that review is the only control left.
findings.evidence: probe1.mts case A: import MUE_2026Q3.csv for 2026-07-01..2026-09-30, raise to L2 and set every record to 2026-10-01..2026-12-31. checkContentSet(drafts) returns [], and assembleRelease({release:1}) returns 'assembled content/outgoing/1'.
findings.fix: In checkRecord for real sets, for pfs_rvu, pfs_gpci and ncci_mue, run statedQuarter(type, {fileName: basename(source.path), url: source.url, text: stored source text}) through the existing sourceReader. Refuse when it returns null or throws, when windowQuarter(record) differs from it, or when it states an effective day the window does not start on. This is an added refusal under the same exception. Cache it per source.path. Add a test with a re-dated MUE file.

verdict.reason:
The code behaves as the finding says, but the finding misreads the design, so it is not a major. At 45fe117f, tools/verify-content/check.ts:213-240 (statedWindowProblems) checks three things: that a quarterly window lies inside some quarter (C1), that ZIP quotes state the window's YYYYQ (C3), and that quarterly records are never hand-typed (C15). C16 is in checkContentSet. Nothing in checkRecord (:242-283) reads the file's stated quarter for pfs_rvu, pfs_gpci or ncci_mue. Nothing in the record ties its window to the source either: verificationSchema (packages/rules/src/schema.ts:498) holds only level, by, on and questions, with no hash of the record. So the probe's path holds (scratchpad review-probes/probe1.mts:70). Raise an imported Q3 MUE draft to L2, re-date every record to Q4, and it passes, because all of its records still share one window.

The finding's basis is wrong, though. The sentence 'the window is cross-checked against the quarter the file states' is the 'R2 (importer and parsers)' bullet in design 2.2 (lane-b-release-content-checks.md:130-135). The separate 'R2 (checker)' bullet (:136-140) and the exact contract in 5.3 (:732-756) scope the checker to C1, C2, C3, C15 and C16. Its stated goal is only that no record widens a content's span beyond a quarter. Reading the stated quarter in the checker was never asked for, so the PR matches the reviewed design. This is not a design requirement that is missing.

The case also needs someone to edit an approved draft by hand on purpose, against the stated rule 'import it again rather than editing a record's dates'. It also needs a named L2 sign-off and pull-request review, and the record still shows its source.path and source.url (for example MUE_2026Q3.csv) next to the edited window, so a reviewer can see the mismatch. It is a real defense-in-depth gap: MUE unit caps can affect money in another quarter, and the checker could close it cheaply. Being outside the design and needing deliberate human action plus a sign-off makes it a minor improvement, not a major.
verdict.betterFix: Take this as an 'improve as you go' added refusal, under #30's checker exception: it only adds refusals. In checkRecord, for real sets and quarterly types other than the ZIP types (C3 already covers those), run the importer's exported statedQuarter(type, {fileName: basename(source.path), url: source.url, text}) on the stored source. Do it through sourceReader, memoized per source.path, and decode the text only once. Refuse when it returns null or throws, when windowQuarter(from, to) differs from the stated quarter, or when the file states an effective day and the window does not start on it. That makes the checker match importer rules I2/I3/I5/I7. Before turning it on, confirm that the real drafts at 6ddd587 all pass, so no record that passes today is refused. Write the new problem strings and a test into 5.3 as C17, with a re-dated MUE draft and a re-dated GPCI draft whose stated quarter comes only from the URL. Separately, consider binding the L2 sign-off to a hash of the record's key, value and window, so that any edit after sign-off is refused whatever the field.

findings.title: COVERAGE.md withdrawn entries typed by hand into an outgoing release pass the checker, and duplicate JSON keys let what a reviewer reads differ from what is parsed
findings.problem: The checker accepts any withdrawn entry in a numbered release's COVERAGE.md that matches a computed loss and carries two different names. The drafts note and the assembler are optional for that path. A hand-made content/outgoing/N, with its manifest resealed (anyone can recompute it), hides a coverage loss behind invented signers. The only remaining guard is the founder's review under `* @PureTideWater`. readJsonBlock uses JSON.parse, which keeps the last of duplicate keys. A block holding `"withdrawn": []` near the top and the real list further down shows a reviewer an empty withdrawal in the diff, while the checker uses the later list.
findings.evidence: probe1.mts case C: copy outgoing/1 to outgoing/2 without the Q3 file, write a COVERAGE.md whose 12 withdrawn entries are signed 'Any One' / 'Any Two', and run sealRelease. checkContentSet(outgoing/2) returns []. With a duplicate leading '"withdrawn": []' it still returns [].
findings.fix: Refuse duplicate keys in readJsonBlock: parse with a reviver or a scan that rejects a repeated key, as an added refusal. In RELEASE.md and COVERAGE.md's prose, render the withdrawn entries verbatim so the reviewer reads exactly what is parsed. Optionally make the checker require that a release with withdrawn entries deletes content/drafts/COVERAGE-WITHDRAWN.md in the same PR (git-aware, in CI).

verdict.reason:
Partly real. Minor is the right severity, but only the duplicate-key and prose half is a defect.

(1) Invented signers. A hand-made content/outgoing/N whose COVERAGE.md lists signed withdrawn entries passes the checker. That is the design working as written, not a defect. coverageProblems (tools/verify-content/check.ts:514-602) only checks three things about a withdrawn entry: it equals a computed unexplained loss (C11/C12), its two names differ when trimmed and case-folded (records.ts:652-653), and withdrawn_on is not after prepared_on (C13). The design says the names catch "a slip and nothing more: one person can type two names", and that the real second signature is the founder's code-owner review (`.github/CODEOWNERS` `*`) (design section 4, ADR 0071 paragraph, lines 439-441). A hand-made outgoing release still lands through a pull request under that same review. So there is no fail-open beyond what the design accepted.

(2) Duplicate keys and prose. This part is real and is a gap against the design's contract:
- readJsonBlock (packages/rules/src/records.ts:771) calls JSON.parse, which silently keeps the last of duplicate keys.
- The checker never compares the file to the canonical text. The design (5.1, "COVERAGE.md's text (byte-exact, from renderCoverageFile)") and the file's own words ("never edit it by hand", records.ts:735) say the file is exactly what renderCoverageFile emits. Yet check.ts:527-535 only parses the block against the schema.
- So a file with a leading "withdrawn": [] and a later real list passes. So does a prose bullet changed to read "0 withdrawn by a signed note" over a block holding 12 entries.

The concealment is weak: the diff still shows the second list, and the founder reviews it. That is why this stays minor rather than major. The finding is right that what a reviewer skims (the prose counts, the first key) can differ from what is enforced.

The finding's proposed fix is narrower than needed. A duplicate-key reviver alone leaves the prose drift open. Requiring the drafts note to be deleted needs git awareness the checker does not have.
verdict.betterFix: Add one refusal after the schema parse in coverageProblems (check.ts, just after line 535): if readFileSync(file) !== renderCoverageFile(parsed.data), push "COVERAGE.md is not exactly what pnpm release:assemble writes: re-run it, never edit the file by hand". This enforces the design's byte-exact contract (5.1). It also refuses duplicate keys, reordered keys and edited prose counts all at once, and it stays an added refusal inside #30's exception: the assembler already writes renderCoverageFile output, so genuine releases pass. Optionally, make readJsonBlock refuse a repeated key in the same object, so the drafts note (COVERAGE-WITHDRAWN.md, whose prose is free) is also protected. Add a test for each refusal: a duplicated "withdrawn" key, and a prose count edited to 0.

findings.title: Quarter patterns use \b, which treats '_' as a word character, so common CMS-style names state no quarter
findings.problem: `\bRVU(\d{2})([A-D])\b`, `(20\d{2})[ _-]?Q([1-4])\b`, `\b(JAN|...)` and `\bEff...\s+` all fail when the token touches an underscore, and the Eff form also needs whitespace. The importer then refuses with I2. This fails closed, but realistic names are refused and operators are pushed to rename files.
findings.evidence: probe2.mts: statedQuarter('pfs_gpci', {fileName:'GPCI2026.csv', url:'.../rvu26d_updated.zip'}) gives null. 'MUE_PRACTITIONER_2026Q4_v2.csv' gives null. 'MCR_MUE_PractitionerServices_Eff_10-01-2026.csv' gives null. By contrast, 'rvu26d-updated.zip' gives 2026-Q4.
findings.fix: Use alphanumeric lookarounds (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) and (?![A-Za-z0-9]) in place of \b, and allow [ _:.-] after 'Eff'. This only adds patterns, which the design permits.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds, and minor is the right severity. I checked QUARTER_PATTERNS in packages/rules/src/import.ts at 45fe117f (lines 110-117). They use \b, and JavaScript counts '_' as a word character, so a token that touches an underscore never matches. The Eff pattern also needs \s+ after 'Eff'. I ran a probe (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6dcacc47-f55b-5ed0-ab9e-d8b495c8bdd9/scratchpad/review-probes/int5.mts) against statedQuarter at 45fe117f:
- the URL .../rvu26d_updated.zip gives null
- 'MUE_PRACTITIONER_2026Q4_v2.csv' gives null
- 'MCR_MUE_PractitionerServices_Eff_10-01-2026.csv' gives null
- the URL .../rvu26d-updated.zip gives 2026-Q4

I also found a case the finding missed: the URL .../rvu24ar.zip gives null, because the trailing R after the quarter letter blocks the closing \b. CMS uses that 'AR' suffix for revised releases. When statedQuarter returns null, refuseUndatedWindow (lines 200-206) throws the I2 'quarter_unstated' refusal before anything is stored, so the importer fails closed. No unchecked content loads and no money is wrong, so it is not a blocker or a major. What it does cause is wrong refusals of plausible CMS file and zip names, and the operator has to rename the file.

One part of the evidence is weak. 'GPCI2026.csv' states no quarter at all, so null is correct for that name; that case only fails because of the rvu26d_updated URL.

The design calls these patterns the contract until a real download shows what CMS writes, and it allows later pull requests to add patterns. So this is a gap in a contract that is still provisional, not a design violation.
verdict.betterFix: Replace every \b with alphanumeric lookarounds (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) and (?![A-Za-z0-9]), so that '_', '-', '.' and the ends of the name all count as separators. Allow an optional revision suffix on the RVU token: /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])RVU(\d{2})([A-D])R?(?![A-Za-z0-9])/gi. Allow the Eff separator to be [\s_:.-]+ rather than only \s+. Keep the two-quarter and not-a-date refusals unchanged, since this only adds matches. Add one positive test for each of these names: rvu26d_updated.zip, rvu24ar.zip, MUE_PRACTITIONER_2026Q4_v2.csv and MCR_MUE_PractitionerServices_Eff_10-01-2026.csv. Add negative tests to confirm the change opens nothing it should not: 'XRVU26D' and 'RVU26DX' must not match, and a name that states two quarters, such as RVU26D_2026Q3, must still be refused. Record the added patterns in content/sources/README.md beside the list given in the I2 message.

verdict.reason: This holds as stated. Design 5.6.7 (lane-b-release-content-checks.md:1060) asks for `readonly contentNotLoaded: boolean`, so the build does not match the design. The code comment says an absent value is "for callers that judge lines no release priced". No such caller exists: judgeLine returns early unless there is a shortfall from a priced variance, so every judged line was priced under some release. Today's production paths all set the field. execute.ts:316 sets it in candidateLines. report/content.ts:503 sets it, and its `trace !== null &&` guard is a separate edge case. findings.title: A month whose run failed release_read_outside_fetch is planned again on every monitoring trigger
findings.problem: A read outside the fetch is a deterministic PaidWhole defect. The run fails as release_read_outside_fetch, and the failure text tells a person to create a new run once it is fixed. But uncoveredMonths() (apps/worker/src/monitor/plan.ts:117-138) treats every failed run as not covering its month. contentFailure() and waitingOnLocation() do not match this code. So each upload chain and each daily monitoring run creates a new run for the month, prices it in full, rolls it back, and logs RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH again. This loop is loud, not silent. But it is the kind of repeat the content wait was designed to avoid, and its cost grows with the month's size (5.10).
findings.evidence: plan.ts:301-307: only location and content failures put a month in a waiting list. Every other failure falls through to createPricingRun. execute.ts:393-398 fails the run with 'release_read_outside_fetch'.
findings.fix: Either list such months as waiting until the release in force or ENGINE_VERSION changes (the same fragment as the content wait), or record in the design that a daily retry is intended until the defect is fixed.

verdict.reason:
The mechanism is real at 45fe117f, but the cost is overstated and the severity should be nit, not minor.

- **What holds.** uncoveredMonths() (apps/worker/src/monitor/plan.ts:117-138) excludes only runs with status <> 'failed'. In planMonitoring() (plan.ts:288-307) only waitingOnLocation() and contentFailure() can hold a month back, and contentFailure() matches only CONTENT_FAILURE_CODES. So after execute.ts:394-397 fails a run as release_read_outside_fetch, the next trigger (an upload's chain or the daily monitoring schedule) creates a new run for that month. Unless code changes, that run throws again and logs RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH again.
- **Cost is overstated.** The finding says each retry "prices it in full". It does not. The throw is per batch (execute.ts:366-371: `if (violation || view.violation !== null) throw new ReadOutsideFetch`), and it fires right after the first batch whose view saw a lookup outside the fetch. The run stops there, not at the end of the month. Unlike location or content stops, it does not price on to the end.
- **Reachability.** No customer input reaches this path. It fires only when PaidWhole's key derivation has a bug, which the design calls PaidWhole's own defect that must never hide (design 5.6.2, "Precedence"). Retrying is also how the code already treats the other non-waiting failure codes (job_failed, engine_version_mismatch, unmapped_plan).
- **No requirement missed.** The design's "No daily loop" (5.6.3, lines 977-979) covers only the content-waiting months. It says nothing about waiting on release_read_outside_fetch. The outer catch for ReadOutsideFetch (design lines 937-938) is built exactly as written.
- **Retrying has an upside.** The error repeats each day until the defect is fixed, and once a fixed build is deployed the month prices by itself. That is arguably better than a silent wait.
- **The one real inconsistency is text.** The failure text (apps/web/src/components/pricing/display.tsx:46) tells a person to "create a new run once it is fixed", while the monitor will in fact re-run the month itself.

So: no wrong money, no check that fails open, no freeze broken. It is a design-consistency and wording point on a path only a code bug can reach.
verdict.betterFix:
Do not add a new wait predicate. A wait keyed on the release in force would wrongly hold a month after a code fix ships with no new release. A wait keyed on ENGINE_VERSION would miss fixes outside packages/pricing (the key derivation lives in the worker), and packages/pricing is frozen. Keep the daily retry, and make it intended and accurate:
1. Add one sentence to design 5.6.3 and ADR 0071: a month whose run failed release_read_outside_fetch is planned again at each trigger. It fails at its first violating batch and logs RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH each time until the defect is fixed, then prices by itself.
2. Reword FAILURE_TEXT.release_read_outside_fetch in display.tsx:46 to something like "...so no line was kept and the operator was alerted; the month is priced again by itself once it is fixed."
Optionally, add a monitor test that pins this: a month whose last run failed release_read_outside_fetch gets a new run, and is not listed in waitingOnContent.

findings.title: "What this release covers" drops any family that is not loaded
findings.problem: The card only lists families that are open or have a through date (`.filter((family) => family.open || family.through !== null)`). A family the release in force does not load at all (for example no ncci_mue records), or loads only for future days, never appears. The customer reads a list that looks complete and cannot see the gap. Design 5.8.6 and runbook section 6 say the card lists each family of the release in force. RCC-08 says customers see each family's loaded-through date.
findings.evidence: releases/page.tsx:70 filters out `loaded:false` and `through:null && !open` rows from familiesLoadedThrough(); content-through.ts:123-127 returns those rows with through null. docs/runbooks/content-updates.md:112 says "lists each family of the release in force". No test asserts the Releases route or page output (git grep finds no test using loadedThrough or "What this release covers" outside content-through.db.test).
findings.fix: Render the families that are not loaded as "<title>: not loaded" (and "<title>: loaded from <date>" for future-only), or say in the card that it lists only the loaded families. Add a releases-route db test that asserts loadedThrough.

verdict.reason: The finding holds as stated. At 45fe117f, releases.ts:86 builds loadedThrough from familiesLoadedThrough(windows, today). That function (content-through.ts:123) returns a row for every family on the calendar except the on_change ones, and it does not filter rows. familyLoadedThrough (packages/rules/src/calendar.ts:412-426) returns {through:null, open:false, loaded:false} for a family with any content missing. It returns {through:null, open:false, loaded:true} for a family loaded only for days after today. releases/page.tsx:70 then keeps only `family.open || family.through !== null`, so both kinds of row are dropped without any sign on the page. The path is reachable: any release in force that lacks records for a calendar family (an early release without NCCI/MUE content, for example) yields loaded:false for that family, and the card titled "What this release covers" lists the other families as if the list were complete. The customer page shows nothing else about the gap; only the Coverage banner speaks, and only for the fee schedule. The Content due view that would show it is console-only. Runbook section 6 says the page "lists each family of the release in force", and RCC-08 says customers see each family's loaded-through date. The page does not do that for families that are not loaded. Design 5.8.6 never says how to show a family that is not loaded, so this is partly a gap in the design, not a plain departure from it. Minor is the right severity: no amount is computed wrongly, pricing is not affected (unpriced reasons still cover lines with no content), and nothing fails open. The defect is a completeness and trust problem in what customers are told. The test gap is also accurate: content-through.db.test.ts covers familiesLoadedThrough itself, but no test renders the page or checks how it filters these rows.
verdict.betterFix: Keep every row from familiesLoadedThrough in the card. Render loaded:false as "<title>: not loaded in this release". Render loaded:true with through null and open false as "<title>: loaded from a later date" (or give the first loaded day, if the type exposes it). Change the runbook section 6 and design 5.8.6 wording to name all three forms. Then add a releases-route db test, against a synthetic release that lacks one family, asserting the not-loaded row is in ReleasesPageData.loadedThrough, and a page or e2e assertion that the card shows it.

findings.title: Truncation note claims the CLI prints the full body; nothing does
findings.problem: When a body passes 6,000 characters, its last line says `pnpm exec tsx tools/content-calendar/index.ts` "prints it whole". The CLI writes the same bounded bodies to the findings file, and its stdout prints only a count (index.ts:86). The summary holds only titles. No output carries the full body.
findings.evidence: render.ts:30-38 bounded() is applied in dueBody/sourceBody, findingsJson writes those bounded bodies, index.ts:84-86 writes findings and summary and prints `content-calendar: N findings`.
findings.fix: Change the wording (for example "...cut at 6,000 characters; the entry's source page and the runbook hold the rest"), or add a flag that prints unbounded bodies.

verdict.reason: The finding holds at 45fe117f. render.ts:16 defines CUT as "...`pnpm exec tsx tools/content-calendar/index.ts` prints it whole." bounded() (render.ts:30-38) adds that line to every body over MAX_BODY (6,000). Both body builders call it: dueBody at :68 and sourceBody at :90. findings() (:94-102) keeps only these cut bodies. findingsJson (:105-107) writes them as they are. summaryMarkdown (:110-121) writes only titles. index.ts:84-86 writes those two files and prints only "content-calendar: N findings on DATE" to stdout. The CLI has no flag that prints bodies uncut: parseArgs at index.ts:39 accepts only today, out, summary and no-fetch. So the command the note points to never shows the rest of the body, and someone who follows it gets the same cut text or a count. Real inputs reach this path. In a source_unrecorded or source_changed finding, sourceBody lists one code-span line per new file name (:81), so a source page that links a few hundred matching files goes past 6,000 characters. No money, gate or PHI is involved: the issue misdirects a person to a command that cannot help. Minor is the right severity.
verdict.betterFix: Make the note point to places that really hold the rest, and say how much was cut. For example: "The rest of this finding (N more lines) was cut at 6,000 characters; the source page (<page>) lists every file, and docs/runbooks/content-updates.md says what to do." The note should not name a command that does not print the body. If a full copy is worth keeping, have the CLI write each uncut body to a file passed with --full <dir>, uploaded as a workflow artifact, and name that artifact in the note. Do not print the bodies to stdout, where they would land in the job log. findings.title: Windows-query over-budget advisory never reaches the notify issue
findings.problem: Design 5.9 says a cold windows-query time above the 5 s budget appears as a headed line in the run's summary and in the notify issue's body. notify runs only on `failure()`, and its body is a fixed sentence. So an over-budget time on a passing run gets only a ::warning annotation and a summary line: no issue, and nothing in the body.
findings.evidence: release-capacity.yml:95 `if: failure() && ...`. :108 body is a constant. checks.ts:174-179 puts the overage in advisories, which never fail the run. run.ts:531-533 emits it only as a ::warning.
findings.fix: Have the capacity job write an advisories output (or a file artifact). Let notify also run on success when advisories exist, opening or commenting on the issue with the advisory line. Alternatively record a design deviation in ADR 0071.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at 45fe117f. The design (lane-b-release-content-checks.md, 5.9, around line 1581) says a cold windows-query time above the 5 s budget is "a headed line in the run's summary and in the notify issue's body, not a failure". The summary half is built: checks.ts:199 adds an "Advisory:" section to summary.md, and run.ts:524-525 appends it to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. The issue half is not. checks.ts:174-180 puts the overage only in `advisories`, and `pass` depends on `reasons` alone, so run.ts:534 returns 0 and the capacity job passes. notify (release-capacity.yml:95) runs only on `failure() && github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, so a passing run with an over-budget time opens no issue. Even when the run fails for another reason, the body at :108 is a fixed sentence that never names the advisory. The only other signal is the ::warning annotation at run.ts:531-533, which nobody is notified about on a weekly scheduled run. The design partly causes this: its own 5.10 (around line 1677) specifies notify as `if: failure() && ...`, which conflicts with 5.9, and the builder followed 5.10. Still, 5.9's requirement is unmet and ADR 0071 records no deviation. Minor fits: the time is advisory under the founder's ruling, so no money, content or failing check is involved. Only the alerting for a performance regression is lost.
verdict.betterFix: In the capacity job, after run.ts, write the advisories (code-built strings of IDs and numbers only) as a job output. One way: run.ts writes `advisories=<joined>` to GITHUB_OUTPUT, or the step reads the list from release-capacity.json with jq. Declare `outputs: advisories:` on the capacity job. Change notify to `if: always() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (needs.capacity.result == 'failure' || needs.capacity.outputs.advisories != '')`. Pass the advisories into the step through `env:` (never inline `${{ }}` in `run:`, to avoid script injection). Add an "Advisory:" headed section to the body. On a passing run with advisories, comment on the open release-capacity issue or open one, so a failure issue's title does not mislead. Fix design 5.10's notify condition to match, or record the narrower behaviour as a deviation in ADR 0071.

findings.title: "Ended" row says later lines wait for the content; most families do not wait
findings.problem: The runbook says that when content ends, "lines on later dates wait for it". Only the MPPR/MUE families make a month wait (waiting_on_content_*). An ended fee schedule leaves lines unpriced NO_PFS_VALUE (no_rvu_in_basis_year). An ended GPCI, conversion factor or locality gives ENGINE_ERROR lines in a complete run. Neither waits or reprices by itself. An operator reading this may think nothing is lost until load.
findings.evidence: ADR 0071 'Months the content does not cover' limits the waiting codes to MPPR/MUE. in-effect.ts:feeSchedulePeriodsNotLoaded reads unpriced lines for the fee-schedule gap. LOUD_CONTENT_TYPES (design 5.6.5) are logged on complete runs.
findings.fix: Reword: "lines on later dates are refused (MPPR, MUE: the month waits) or left unpriced (fee schedule, GPCI, conversion factor, locality) until it is loaded and their months are priced again."

verdict.reason:
I could not refute this. At 45fe117f, docs/runbooks/content-updates.md line 74 (the "Ended" row, title `Content ended:`) says "lines on later dates wait for it". That issue opens for every calendar family. calendar.ts:602 builds the title for any entry, and calendar.test.ts:166 checks it for the fee schedule. The families include fee_schedule, conversion_factor, zip_locality, ncci_ptp, sequestration and others (calendar.ts:16-28, 117-308).

Only three failure codes make a month wait: waiting_on_content_mppr, _mue and _mppr_mue. ADR 0071 "Months the content does not cover" lines 125-133 says so, and apps/worker/src/monitor/plan.ts step 5 holds such a month with no run created. A fee-schedule gap is different. The run completes and the lines are left unpriced NO_PFS_VALUE / no_rvu_in_basis_year (apps/web/src/lib/coverage/in-effect.ts:128-151). A locality-content gap also completes, with the line ENGINE_ERROR (plan.ts step 4 comment, "no_locality_plus_four, whose run completes with the line ENGINE_ERROR"). Plan step 3 plans only months that no queued, running or complete run covers. So when the next release loads, those completed months are not priced again on their own. "Wait" therefore misdescribes both what happens now (lines show unpriced, not held) and what happens next (no automatic repricing).

The row's instruction, "Load the next period now", is still right and urgent. The harm is a wrong mental model: the operator may skip pricing the months again after the load. No money or check is affected, so minor fits.
verdict.betterFix: Reword the row's "What to do" cell to say what happens per family and what the operator must do after loading. For example: "The loaded content has run out. For MPPR and MUE, a month that reads it is refused with no line kept and waits; it is priced again by itself once a release loads that content. For any other family (fee schedule, conversion factor, locality and the rest), the month's run completes with those lines unpriced (NO_PFS_VALUE) or ENGINE_ERROR. Those months are not priced again on their own, so after the release is in force, price them again. Load the next period now." If the team instead wants completed months with content-gap lines to be planned again when a new release is in force, that is a design change (plan.ts step 3), not a runbook fix, and needs its own ruling.

findings.title: Private-repository cost claim ignores that the weekly harness refuses the private 2-CPU runner
findings.problem: ADR 0071 and ci.md say both workflows cost about 1,250 runner minutes a month once private and run "on the free 4-CPU runner". On a private repository `ubuntu-24.04` is the 2-CPU runner. run.ts:354 runnerTooSmall() (the screening layout's requiredCpus) then stops the harness with RUNNER_TOO_SMALL, so the weekly test would fail every week instead of measuring. ci.md:145-148 itself notes that capacity refuses a 2-CPU runner and points at the 8-core runner note.
findings.evidence: release-capacity.yml:32 runs-on: ubuntu-24.04. run.ts:354-357 throws RUNNER_TOO_SMALL. docs/runbooks/ci.md:147-149 places the 1,250-minute line right after "the capacity measurement refuses a 2-CPU runner".
findings.fix: State in ADR 0071 'Revisit when' and ci.md that a private repository needs the larger runner for release-capacity (as screening-capacity's runbook says), and price it, or pick runs-on from github.event.repository.private.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. At 45fe117f, ADR 0071:205-206 says the weekly real-size test runs "on the free 4-CPU runner" and that once the repository is private it costs "at most about 1,250 runner minutes a month". docs/runbooks/ci.md:146-149 gives the same budget, 780 minutes of it for the weekly test. Neither document says the weekly test stops working on a private repository.

The workflow cannot measure on a private repository. .github/workflows/release-capacity.yml:32 is `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` with no switch on `github.event.repository.private`, and that label is the 2-CPU, 8 GB runner on a private repository (ci.md:143 says so itself). tools/release-capacity/run.ts:354-357 calls runnerTooSmall() from tools/screening-capacity/limits.ts:399. That function requires requiredCpus() = sharedLayoutCpus, which is 4 for production's sizes (limits.test.ts:100). limits.test.ts:148 shows a 2-CPU runner gets the result "the runner has 2 CPUs; the test needs 4", so run.ts throws HarnessStop RUNNER_TOO_SMALL before any measurement.

As a result, once the repository is private, the run the ADR calls "#31's only proof that release 1 fits the worker" fails every week within minutes, and the 780-minute figure describes a run that cannot happen. screening-capacity.yml:128-131 records exactly this limit for its own job, so this PR copied the runner without copying the caveat.

Minor is the right severity. The repository is public today, the workflow is not a required check, and it fails loudly rather than open. ADR 0071:257 already lists "the repository turns private" as a revisit trigger, but it only asks to re-read the minutes and does not say the test will be refused. This is a wrong design statement and a known future breakage, not wrong money or a gate that fails open.
verdict.betterFix: In ADR 0071 (the paragraph at 204-208 and the "Revisit when" item at 257) and in docs/runbooks/ci.md:147-149, say that on a private repository release-capacity needs the 8-core runner, as docs/runbooks/screening-capacity.md "The 8-core runner" already says for screening-capacity. Without it the weekly test is refused as RUNNER_TOO_SMALL. Price that runner's billed minutes separately, because larger runners are not covered by the included 3,000 minutes, and remove the weekly test's 780 minutes from the free-runner total. Copy screening-capacity.yml:128-131's comment onto release-capacity.yml:30-32 so the workflow states the same limit. When the repository goes private, the runs-on label should become the 8-core runner, either chosen from `github.event.repository.private` or set by the founder. This should be decided together with screening-capacity's runner so the two jobs do not diverge.

findings.title: Console says "No rule release is published." when releases are published but none is in force
findings.problem: dueContent passes `releases.find((release) => release.inForce)`. If published releases exist but none is in force (for example all withdrawn), releaseNo is null. The page then prints "No rule release is published.", and contentDue's item is titled "No rule release is published", which is false. contentDue also switches to judging the drafts, with "not in the drafts" titles, although releases are published.
findings.evidence: rule-releases.ts:162 and page.tsx:59. calendar.ts:478 `onDrafts = sources.releaseNo === null`.
findings.fix: Tell 'none published' apart from 'none in force' ("No rule release is in force."), and keep judging on the newest published release rather than the drafts in that case.

verdict.reason:
The bad state the finding describes (releases published, none in force, for example all withdrawn) cannot happen. The schema rules it out.

1. `releases[].inForce` is `r.release_no = current_rule_release()` (apps/web/src/lib/releases/queries.ts:41). current_rule_release() is the max published release with no withdrawal (packages/db/migrations/20261019150000_reruns_and_release_withdrawal.sql:49-53). So it is non-null whenever at least one published release is not withdrawn.
2. Withdrawals can never cover every published release:
   - `rule_release_withdrawal.reinstated_release_no` is `integer NOT NULL` (same migration, line 39).
   - The trigger refuses any withdrawal whose `reinstated_release_no IS DISTINCT FROM` the max published, non-withdrawn release below it (lines 65-70).
   - When the release in force is the only published, non-withdrawn one, that max() is NULL. Every allowed (non-null) value is then distinct from NULL, so the insert is refused.
   - The trigger only lets the release in force be withdrawn (lines 62-64).
   - Rows never change or leave (lines 59-61).
3. So the last non-withdrawn release can never be withdrawn. A release published later is itself the max non-withdrawn, so it comes into force.

The invariant follows: if any release is published, exactly one is in force. `releases.find((release) => release.inForce)` (apps/web/src/lib/routes/rule-releases.ts:162) is therefore undefined only when nothing is published. In that case "No rule release is published." (page.tsx:59) and contentDue's switch to the drafts (`onDrafts = sources.releaseNo === null`, packages/rules/src/calendar.ts:478) are both correct. No real caller or input reaches the misleading text.

Leftover: page.tsx and calendar.ts lean on that schema invariant without saying so. That is a readability nit at most, not a minor defect.
verdict.betterFix:
No change is needed. Optionally, for readability:
- Add a one-line comment at rule-releases.ts:162 saying the schema guarantees a release is in force whenever one is published, citing the withdrawal trigger's NOT NULL reinstated_release_no.
- Or make the fact explicit by passing `releases.length === 0` as the "none published" signal.

Do not add a "none in force" branch: it would be dead code for a state the database refuses.

findings.title: release_read_outside_fetch tells the customer the operator was alerted, but nothing alerts
findings.problem: FAILURE_TEXT.release_read_outside_fetch says 'no line was kept and the operator was alerted'. When a price job reads outside its fetch, execute.ts catches ReadOutsideFetch, fails the run and logs at error level with error_code RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH (apps/worker/src/price/execute.ts ~392-397). It then returns { outcome: 'failed' } and does not throw, so pg-boss sees the job succeed and JobFailedOnLastAttempt never fires. No metric filter or alarm anywhere matches RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH or that message. The design's later-PR list (section 7.2, row for infra/lib/constructs/monitoring.ts) does not plan one either: it lists only CONTENT_NOT_LOADED, WAITING_ON_CONTENT and the daily-job codes. On top of that, the monitor plan does not hold the month back. This failure code is neither a content code nor location_not_ready, so contentFailure() returns null, waitingOnLocation() is false, and planMonitoring() creates a new run for the month on every plan. Each new run fails the same way. The audit names this as 'PaidWhole's defect, never hidden', yet it would recur every day with no alarm, while the customer is told someone was alerted.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'OUTSIDE_FETCH|outside the keys' infra .github returns nothing at 45fe117f. The worker log group's filters in infra/lib/constructs/monitoring.ts are Heartbeat (:186), JobFailedOnLastAttempt (:227) and PricingRunEngineErrors (:260). The level=error filter at :373 is on screeningLogGroup only. execute.ts returns { outcome: 'failed', failureCode: 'release_read_outside_fetch' } with no rethrow. plan.ts contentFailure() matches only CONTENT_FAILURE_CODES, and waitingOnLocation() matches only 'location_not_ready'. The design (lane-b-release-content-checks.md:1698) carries the same 'operator was alerted' wording, and section 7.2 (:2046) does not list RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH.
findings.fix: Either add RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH to the later PR's monitoring.ts row (a worker log-group filter on error_code, paging the operator topic) and, until it lands, reword the customer text so it does not claim an alert ('PaidWhole has been told' only once that is true), or have the price job rethrow after failRun so JobFailed fires. Also consider having the monitor plan hold back a month whose newest run failed release_read_outside_fetch under the same release, so the defect does not start a fresh failing run every day.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds at 45fe117f. All of this code is new in the PR: the base 6ddd587 has no release_read_outside_fetch.

1. **The customer text claims an alert.** display.tsx:46 says "the operator was alerted". So does the design's string table (lane-b-release-content-checks.md, about line 1698).

2. **The job looks successful to the queue.** execute.ts:394-397 catches ReadOutsideFetch, runs failRun, logs logger.error with error_code RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH, and returns { outcome: 'failed' } without rethrowing. In price/job.ts, priceHandler only takes the catch/job_failed path when an error is thrown. Here none is, so the handler returns normally, pg-boss marks the job done, and JOB_FAILED_MESSAGE is never logged.

3. **Nothing alarms on that log line.**
   - The worker log group in infra/lib/constructs/monitoring.ts has only these filters: Heartbeat (:186), JobFailedOnLastAttempt (:227), PricingRunEngineErrors (:260, matched on msg), and the model-budget error_codes (:295).
   - The level=error / RUN_FAILED_ERROR_CODES filter (:373) is on screeningLogGroup only, and RUN_FAILED_ERROR_CODES is just ['PRICING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED'] (infra/lib/screening.ts:67).
   - Design §7.2's monitoring.ts row lists CONTENT_NOT_LOADED, WAITING_ON_CONTENT and the CONTENT_* daily codes, not RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH. So no later PR is planned to add one either.

4. **The month starts a new failing run every plan.** In plan.ts, uncoveredMonths treats failed runs as not covering (:131). waitingOnLocation (:170-173) only matches location_not_ready. contentFailure (:221-232) only matches CONTENT_FAILURE_CODES. So planMonitoring (:296-310) goes on to createPricingRun for the month each time. The read-outside-fetch is a deterministic code defect, so each new run under the same release and engine fails the same way: silent, and repeated on every monitor plan.

**Why major and not blocker:** the guard fails closed. No line is kept and no money is wrong. But a requirement the audit states ("PaidWhole's defect, never hidden") is not met, and customer-facing text makes a false claim.

**Refinement:** the path is reachable only through a defect in how keys are fetched. That defect is exactly what this guard exists to catch, so the missing alert is the core of the problem, not a side issue.
verdict.betterFix:
Do not rethrow. A rethrow retries a deterministic failure three times, and then job.ts's failRun overwrites the precise code with job_failed. Instead:

**In this PR (monitoring.ts is a #42 file, so it cannot change here):**
- Reword FAILURE_TEXT.release_read_outside_fetch, and the design's string table, so it does not claim an alert. For example: "The price job read rule content it had not fetched, which is PaidWhole's defect, so no line was kept; create a new run once it is fixed." Restore "the operator was alerted" once the alarm ships.
- Add a §7.2 row for infra/lib/constructs/monitoring.ts and its test: a worker log-group metric filter on $.error_code = 'RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH' (or on the exact message, put in a constant in infra/lib/jobs.ts as PRICING_ENGINE_ERRORS_MESSAGE is), threshold 1, alarm action to the operator page topic.

**In planMonitoring (plan.ts):** hold a month back the way waitingOnLocation does. If the newest run of exactly that month failed release_read_outside_fetch under the current release_no and engine version, add it to a 'held for operator' list instead of creating a new run each plan. A new release or engine version lets it run again.

**Tests:** add a db test showing that a second plan creates no run for that month.

findings.title: Content refusals and waiting months raise no alarm until the later PR
findings.problem: A run refused as waiting_on_content_* is failed, not complete, so PRICING_ENGINE_ERROR (which counts only complete runs) does not fire for it. The CONTENT_NOT_LOADED warn and the monitor's WAITING_ON_CONTENT warn have no metric filter yet. Until the later PR merges, a month blocked on unloaded MPPR or MUE content is visible only on the customer's Coverage card. The 'engine-error page stays' argument covers complete runs with stopped lines, not refused runs. This is documented in the design (7.2), so it is minor, but it is a window with no operator signal.
findings.evidence: execute.ts ContentNotLoaded branch: failRun(error.code) plus logger.warn(CONTENT_NOT_LOADED_MESSAGE). The operatorAlerts() engine-error log runs only when outcome === 'complete'. infra/lib/jobs.ts:27-37 defines only the constants. monitoring.ts has no filter on CONTENT_NOT_LOADED or WAITING_ON_CONTENT.
findings.fix: Name this window in the PR description and runbook (docs/runbooks/content-updates.md): until the alarm PR, check the worker logs for CONTENT_NOT_LOADED daily. Or land the CONTENT_NOT_LOADED metric filter first, as soon as #42 merges.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds at 45fe117f, and minor is the right severity. In apps/worker/src/price/execute.ts:404-408, a ContentNotLoaded refusal calls failRun(error.code), writes a warn-level CONTENT_NOT_LOADED log line and returns { outcome: 'failed' } without throwing. Two things follow:
(a) The PRICING_ENGINE_ERROR log (lines 413-416) runs only when outcome === 'complete', so it never fires for a refused run.
(b) The job does not throw, so the worker's JOB_FAILED_MESSAGE is never logged and the JobFailedOnLastAttempt alarm (infra/lib/constructs/monitoring.ts:217-257) stays quiet too.
infra/lib/jobs.ts:27-37 only defines CONTENT_NOT_LOADED_MESSAGE and CONTENT_NOT_LOADED_METRIC. monitoring.ts imports only the JOB_FAILED and PRICING_ENGINE_ERRORS constants (line 18), so neither CONTENT_NOT_LOADED nor the monitor's WAITING_ON_CONTENT warn (apps/worker/src/monitor/job.ts:66-73) has a metric filter. Until the later PR, a month refused as waiting_on_content_* reaches no operator alarm at all.

It stays minor because it is not a regression in money or in alerting for the main case. Before this PR, such a line was priced without the MPPR or MUE limit, looked right and raised no alert. Now the money is withheld and the month waits, which fails closed. Design 7.2 and ADR 0071 (lines 145-151, 213) document the window and put the alarm in #42's monitoring.ts.

The finding does miss one narrower point, which strengthens it a little without changing the severity. findings.title: Source watch fails open on new files whose names are not plain
findings.problem: pageFileNames throws away any decoded name outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,120}. It only adds it to a page-wide notShown count. watchSources (lines 121-131) then matches filePattern against the kept names only. So a new period's file whose link name has a space, a parenthesis or a percent-encoded character never counts as an added file. No source_changed finding is raised, and no issue says that anything was hidden. The m6 rule was meant to stop such names being shown, but it also stops them being detected. Once knownFiles is recorded, a new quarter's files under a name like that go unreported.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6dcacc47-f55b-5ed0-ab9e-d8b495c8bdd9/scratchpad/review-probes/cc/probe.mts used entry filePattern '^RVU\d{2}[A-D].*\.zip$' and knownFiles ['RVU26A.zip']. The page linked /f/RVU26A.zip, /f/RVU27A%20updated.zip and /f/RVU27B(1).zip. watchSources returned [] (no finding at all), although two new matching files were on the page.
findings.fix: Test filePattern against every decoded link name, plain or not. Count the new names that match but are not plain as part of the change: raise source_changed when added plain names + hidden matching new names > 0, and have the body say '<k> new matching file names were not shown because ...'. To track them in knownFiles without showing them, record a hash or the raw name. Add a test with a %20 and a parenthesised name.

verdict.reason:
This holds at 45fe117f. In tools/content-calendar/fetch.ts, lines 68-72 keep only names that match PLAIN_NAME. Every other decoded name only adds 1 to a page-wide notShown count. Line 122 tests entry.filePattern against seen.names, the plain names only, and line 129 raises source_changed only when the plain added list is non-empty. A new file whose decoded name has a space, a parenthesis or another character outside the plain set is therefore never compared against filePattern. It produces no finding. The notShown count goes nowhere either, because it is carried only on a finding that something else raised (render.ts:83-84).

I re-ran the probe at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6dcacc47-f55b-5ed0-ab9e-d8b495c8bdd9/scratchpad/review-probes/cc/probe.mts against HEAD 45fe117f. It used the real PFS entry's pattern '^RVU\d{2}[A-D].*\.zip$' (packages/rules/src/calendar.ts:130) with knownFiles ['RVU26A.zip']. With the page linking /f/RVU27A%20updated.zip and /f/RVU27B(1).zip, the output was "non-plain new files -> []". Real calendar entries reach this path: the PFS, ZIP, MPPR, MUE and PTP entries all carry a filePattern.

The code follows design section 5.8.3 as written (only plain names are kept, then filePattern is compared). So this is a gap in the design itself, not the PR departing from it. The fix needs a short amendment to 5.8.3 as well as the code change.

Major is the right severity, not blocker. The source watch is an early warning only. It gives no price and loads no content. The calendar's due-date findings (DUE_STAGES) still fire whatever the fetch result, so a missed source change cannot let content load or price unchecked. But for the cases above it is a check that fails open: a new quarter's file goes unreported with no sign that anything was hidden.

A second, smaller point backs this up. notShown counts every link name on the page that is not plain, including mailto: and javascript: links and paths like '/about%20us' (the probe's noise case gives notShown 3 with no file links at all). Even when it is printed, it says nothing about whether a matching file was hidden.
verdict.betterFix:
Split detection from display.

1. In pageFileNames, return every decoded link name as `all` and also the plain subset.
2. In watchSources, test filePattern against `all`. Compare those against knownFiles using the raw decoded names. knownFiles is repository JSON, not an issue body, so it can hold raw names; no hash is needed, and the operator can record exactly what the page shows.
3. Raise source_changed when any matching name, plain or not, is new.
4. List only the plain new names, in code spans. Replace the page-wide notShown with hiddenMatching: the number of new matching names that are not plain. Render "<k> new matching file names were not shown because they hold characters other than letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen."
5. Do the same for source_unrecorded: count hidden matching names, not page noise.
6. Amend design 5.8.3 to say this.
7. Add tests. A page with RVU27A%20updated.zip and RVU27B(1).zip and knownFiles ['RVU26A.zip'] must give one source_changed with names [] and hiddenMatching 2. A page whose only non-plain links are mailto: and javascript: must give no finding and a count of 0. Keep the hostile-href test asserting that none of those names reaches a body.

findings.title: Only double-quoted hrefs are read; a page redesign silently disables the watch
findings.problem: The href regex accepts only href="...". Single-quoted and unquoted attributes give no names. Names that left the page are not findings (line 96), so a page that switches quoting, or moves its files to sub-pages, makes every entry with knownFiles report nothing, forever. Nothing tells anyone the watch has gone blind.
findings.evidence: Probe: pageFileNames(`x y`) returned {"names":[],"notShown":0}.
findings.fix: Accept href='...' and unquoted href values. Also raise a finding when an entry's knownFiles is non-empty but the page now shows no name matching filePattern ('the source page no longer lists any matching file: the watch cannot see it').

verdict.reason:
The finding is real, and minor is the right severity. At 45fe117f, tools/content-calendar/fetch.ts:63 reads links only with /href\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"/gi. A single-quoted or unquoted href gives no name, so the probe result ({names:[], notShown:0}) is correct from the code alone. Once an entry records knownFiles (fetch.ts:127-131), only names added to the page raise a finding. Names that leave the page raise nothing, as the comment at lines 94-97 says. So if the page switches its quoting, or moves its files to a sub-page, `matching` becomes empty, `added` is empty, and the watch says nothing on every run. No finding states that the page now lists no matching file.

Three things narrow it, which is why it is minor and not major:
(1) The code follows the reviewed design exactly. Design 5.8.x, lines 1373 and 1382, specify "every `href="…"`" and "Names that left the page are not findings". So this is a gap in the design, not a deviation from it, and the fix needs a design amendment, not only a code change.
(2) The failure cannot happen today. Every calendar entry ships with knownFiles: null (packages/rules/src/calendar.ts:131-304, asserted at calendar.test.ts:73). In that state fetch.ts:123-125 raises source_unrecorded on every run, even when it finds zero names. A reviewer recording knownFiles from a page that already uses single quotes would see an empty list, so going blind needs a later redesign of the page.
(3) The watch is advisory: missing a new file delays an issue, not a price. Rules 1-4 still hold, nothing loads unchecked and no amount changes.

Still, the watch exists to say when a source changed (audit #59). Silence that looks the same as "no change" is the fail-open shape, so the gap should be closed.
verdict.betterFix:
First amend the design (line 1373 and the 1382 bullet), then change fetch.ts:
(a) Match href values in all three forms with /href\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|([^\s"'<>`=]+))/gi, taking the first group that is set. The PLAIN_NAME filter still guards what reaches issue bodies.
(b) Add a fourth finding kind, source_lost. It fires when an entry has filePattern set, a non-empty knownFiles, and none of its knownFiles is among the matching names the page now shows. Title: `Content source no longer lists its files: ${title}`; body: the watch cannot see this source, so review the page and update knownFiles.
This keeps "a removed name alone is not a finding" while catching the blind state, which is the losing of every recorded name.
Tests: a single-quoted page, an unquoted page, and a page that lost every recorded name must each give the expected finding, and the existing hostile-href test must still pass with the new forms. Update SOURCE_FINDINGS and render.ts to handle the new kind.

findings.title: Redirects are followed to any host and to plain http
findings.problem: The calendar schema requires https pages (calendar.ts:40). But httpFetcher uses redirect:'follow' and never checks response.url. A redirect to http:// on another host (from a compromised CMS page, an open redirect, or a DNS answer) is fetched, and its link names are reported as the source page's. With plain http, any on-path network attacker can then inject names. The m6 filter limits the damage to plain names in code spans, but issues can still claim a new period's files are out when they are not.
findings.evidence: Probe: httpFetcher('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/redir'), answered with 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/other, returned status 200 and the other page's text. Nothing checks the final URL or its scheme.
findings.fix: Use redirect:'manual' and follow at most a few hops yourself, keeping only https and the hosts the calendar names (www.cms.gov, www.federalregister.gov, x12.org). Or check response.url after the fetch: protocol https: and hostname in that allowlist, otherwise treat the page as unreachable. Add a test.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real as stated. At 45fe117f, tools/content-calendar/fetch.ts:41 calls fetch with redirect:'follow', and line 42 returns only status and text. It never looks at response.url. The real caller reaches it: index.ts:9 imports httpFetcher as watchSources' default fetcher, and the .github/workflows/content-calendar.yml:57 run passes the result into issue bodies (lines 91 and on). The https rule is only checked on the calendar entry (packages/rules/src/calendar.ts:40, z.url({protocol:/^https$/}), tested at calendar.test.ts:93). It is not checked on the URL the content finally comes from. Node's fetch (undici) follows a 301 or 302 from https to plain http on any host, so a single redirect hop drops the guarantee the schema implies. readPage (fetch.ts:84) then treats the 2xx as that entry's page.

The impact is a little wider than the finding says, in both directions. Beyond injected names, a forged or downgraded page can also leave out the new files, so a real new period never produces a source_changed finding and the watch stays silent when it should alert. Even so, the watch is advisory. It only opens GitHub issues. It loads no content, prices nothing and touches no PHI. The m6 filter (PLAIN_NAME, fetch.ts:17) keeps mentions, links and backticks out of the issues. Content still goes through /load-release and the content checker. The likely attack also needs the CMS or Federal Register origin to issue the redirect, or an open redirect on that origin. So this is not a blocker or major. Minor fits.
verdict.betterFix: In httpFetcher, after the fetch, refuse the answer unless new URL(response.url).protocol === 'https:' and its hostname is one of the calendar's own source hosts. Build that set from calendar.map(e => new URL(e.source.page).hostname), or pass the original URL's host in, rather than hardcoding a list that drifts. On a mismatch, throw so readPage records source_unreachable. An alternative is redirect:'manual' with at most three hops, applying the same check to each Location. Either way, add a test with a stub Fetcher, or a local server, that redirects to http:// and to a foreign host and expects source_unreachable. Also add a test showing that a same-host https redirect still works.

findings.title: No cap on response size
findings.problem: response.text() reads the whole body, bounded only by the 20 s timeout. A hostile or misbehaving page can stream hundreds of MB into the check job's memory. The job fails closed (a 'check failing' issue), so this is availability only, but the brief asks for size limits.
findings.evidence: fetch.ts:41-42 has no content-length check and no streamed cap. A probe served a 300 MiB body and was cut only by the timeout (DOMException TimeoutError), never by a size limit.
findings.fix: Read response.body as a stream and abort past a cap (for example 5 MiB, well above any CMS listing page). Treat an abort as unreachable.

verdict.reason:
The finding is accurate but rated too high. At 45fe117f, tools/content-calendar/fetch.ts:40-43 does call `await response.text()` with no content-length check and no streamed cap. The only bound is `AbortSignal.timeout(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)`, which is 20 s (line 12). That signal also covers reading the body, so a body is cut off after 20 s and gets one retry (lines 77-90). The attack path, though, is narrow and cannot cause harm:
(1) The URLs are not input. They are constants in packages/rules/src/calendar.ts:105-311 (cms.gov, federalregister.gov, x12.org, ncdoi.gov). To be hostile, a government or standards site would have to be compromised, or a redirect from one would have to be.
(2) The job runs on an ephemeral GitHub `ubuntu-24.04` runner with `timeout-minutes: 15` (.github/workflows/content-calendar.yml:42-43). It holds no PHI, no database and no secrets beyond the workflow token. Memory pressure there harms nothing but that one run.
(3) Every failure path fails closed. A timeout, a network error, or a V8 string-length RangeError on a body over roughly 512M characters is caught at fetch.ts:87 and becomes `source_unreachable`, which is a visible finding. No content loads or prices unchecked, and no check passes falsely.
(4) The design contract (§5.8.3) asks only for `fetcher(url, { timeoutMs: 20_000 })` with one retry. It sets no size limit, so this is not a missing design requirement either.
What is left is a hardening improvement against a misbehaving trusted host. That fits nit, or at most minor, and not anything that blocks the PR.
verdict.betterFix: Optional hardening inside httpFetcher only. The injected Fetcher seam and its tests stay unchanged. Read `response.body` with a reader and keep a byte count. Once the count passes a cap (for example `MAX_PAGE_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024`, an exported constant beside FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS), call `reader.cancel()` and throw, so readPage's existing catch turns it into `source_unreachable`. Also reject early when a `content-length` header is over the cap. Decode with `new TextDecoder().decode(concatenated)`. Add one unit test that drives httpFetcher against a local server streaming a body over the cap and expects a `source_unreachable` finding, with no timeout involved.

findings.title: Findings past 20 are starved while the first 20 stay open
findings.problem: findings() cuts the list to MAX_FINDINGS before the workflow skips issues that are already open (content-calendar.yml:84-90). In the same order every day, the same first 20 findings always win. While those issues stay open, findings 21 and later (the source findings, which come last) are never filed, even though nothing is opened that day. The summary's 'N more findings were left out' line shows only in the step summary, not in an issue.
findings.evidence: render.ts:95-101 slices all findings to 20. The notify loop then skips those whose titles are already in open-titles.txt and creates nothing else. Today's --no-fetch run gives 9 due findings, plus up to 6 source_unrecorded and some unreachable findings. That is close to the cap, and the cap grows with more entries or due stages.
findings.fix: Write every finding (the 6,000-character body cap already bounds each one) and cap the number of issues created per run inside the notify loop, counting only titles not already open. Or pass the open titles into the tool before it slices.

verdict.reason: The finding holds as stated. At 45fe117f, findings() at tools/content-calendar/render.ts:95-101 builds the list with due items first, then source findings, and cuts it with all.slice(0, MAX_FINDINGS), where MAX_FINDINGS is 20 (render.ts:12). This happens before the notify job reads open-titles.txt (content-calendar.yml, the notify step). The notify loop only goes through the findings it was given and skips titles that are already open, so it never moves on to the next finding. The order is fixed every day, so if 20 or more findings come before a given finding and stay open, that finding is never filed. The source findings come last, so they are the ones that get starved. The "N more findings were left out" line goes only to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, so no issue says anything was dropped. The code matches the design: section 3 asks for "a JSON array of at most 20 { title, body }", which is the source of the gap. I ran the tool on 2026-10-26 with --no-fetch: 9 findings (one no-release, seven not-in-drafts, one unreviewed). The cap is not reached yet; with a fetch, adding about 7 source findings still comes in under 20. So the defect is real but not live today. It starts once the calendar or DUE_STAGES grows, or once several entries show up as both due and changed. Minor fits: a missed issue delays a content update, but the step summary still lists every count, and nothing loads or prices content unchecked.
verdict.betterFix: Keep the findings file uncapped: the 6,000-character body cap already bounds each entry, and the GITHUB_OUTPUT base64 size grows only linearly. Move the 20-issue cap into the notify loop and count only issues it actually creates (titles not in open-titles.txt). When findings are left over after the cap, open or update one issue titled "Content calendar: N more findings not filed" that lists the remaining titles, so the overflow shows up in an issue and not only in the step summary. Change the design's line "a JSON array of at most 20" to match, and add a test with 25 findings where the first 20 titles are already open, asserting that findings 21-25 get filed.
